controller_actions.task: Write module.py exposing solve(data) per the user contract. data={'ops':[...]}. Track balance (int) and holds dict id->amount; held=sum of holds; available=balance-held. For each op in order, checks in exactly this order: (1) kind must be one of credit, debit, hold, release else ValueError. (2) for credit/debit/hold, amount must be int >=1 and not bool, else ValueError (missing amount also ValueError). (3) hold: id must not already be an active hold; release: id must be an active hold; else ValueError (a missing id for hold/release: treat release of unknown id as ValueError; hold with missing id is fine to treat as an id of None, or ValueError). (4) debit and hold: amount must not exceed available else ValueError. credit adds to balance; debit subtracts; hold adds hold; release removes hold and ignores any amount field. First failing op raises ValueError, no result returned. Empty ops returns {'balance':0,'held':0,'available':0}. Do not mutate input. Standard library only, no I/O, no dynamic code execution. Handle unhashable ids safely (raise ValueError).

Write test_cases.json: a JSON list of at least 8 distinct cases, each with 'input' ({'ops':[...]}) and exactly one of 'output' (expected result {balance,held,available}) or 'error' ('ValueError'). Match the user contract: kinds credit/debit/hold/release; checks in order: kind valid; amount int>=1 for credit/debit/hold (bool and missing invalid); hold id not already active, release id must be active; debit/hold amount must not exceed available (balance-held). release ignores amount. Empty ops gives zeros. Cover: empty, credit+debit, hold reducing available, release restoring, release ignoring amount (even invalid amount), duplicate hold id error, release unknown id error, debit exceeding available due to hold error, bool amount error, unknown kind error, zero amount error, hold reusable after release, exact-available debit allowed. Ensure expectations are correct.
